rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_API_Loading {
    meta:
        description = "Detects dynamic API loading pattern common in Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        malpedia_reference = "https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.cobalt_strike_beacon"
        malpedia_version = "20260409"
        malpedia_license = "CC BY-NC-SA 4.0"
    strings:
        $s1 = "kernel32" ascii nocase
        $s2 = "ntdll" ascii nocase
        $s3 = "LoadLibrary" ascii nocase
        $s4 = "GetProcAddress" ascii nocase
        $s5 = { 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? E8 ?? ?? ?? ?? 83 C4 08 } // push API hash, push library hash, call
    condition:
        all of ($s1, $s2) and 2 of ($s3, $s4) and $s5
}

arguments.summary: A phishing compromise on WS-FIN-042 (user jsmith) led to execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon via malicious PowerShell launched from Outlook. The attacker performed reconnaissance, established C2 communication over HTTPS, attempted Kerberos-based lateral movement, and accessed a file server via SMB. The initial detection was delayed due to the malware hash being marked as clean in sandbox analysis, though behavioral EDR alerts and IDS signatures were triggered. No containment actions were executed due to misalignment between detection and response tooling.

timeline.description: Legitimate Outlook session started by CORP\jsmith on WS-FIN-042.
Malicious PowerShell process launched from Outlook with encoded command (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011).
IDS triggered on Cobalt Strike C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 (ET TROJAN signature).
Failed Kerberos TGT request to domain controller (indicative of lateral movement attempt).
Successful SMB access to file server WS-FIN-050 (lateral movement confirmed).
Post-exploitation alert generated; incident officially recognized.

}

arguments.summary: A post-exploitation activity alert was triggered on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) belonging to user jsmith@corp.local in the Finance department. Investigation revealed a phishing-induced compromise via malicious Outlook macro spawning encoded PowerShell, which loaded an unsigned DLL via rundll32.exe from the Temp directory. The payload established a Cobalt Strike beacon to C2 at 198.51.100.23:443. Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to 10.0.3.10 and 10.0.5.50. Despite a sandbox marking the sample as 'clean', multiple behavioral and network indicators confirm malicious intent. Response actions were denied due to incorrect targeting on 10.0.5.14 instead of 10.0.5.42.

rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory.

Failed Kerberos TGT request – likely credential brute-force attempt.
Successful SMB access to file server 10.0.5.50 – lateral movement confirmed.
Post-exploitation alert triggered on 10.0.3.190, leading to investigation.
